title: He carried a calling from God…
paragraphs:
He carried a calling from God…
and blood on his hands.

Not a metaphor.
A real body.
A buried secret in the sand.
Moses wasn’t just a leader-in-waiting—he was a fugitive.
Scripture doesn’t hide it.
In Exodus 2:12, he looks both ways… sees no one… and kills an Egyptian.
Then he hides the body.
That’s the résumé of the man God would use to split seas.
Let that sit.
You think your past disqualifies you?

Moses thought the same.
He ran.
Forty years in obscurity.
Dust. Silence. Regret.
But here’s what we miss…

God didn’t call Moses after he cleaned himself up.
God called him while he was still carrying the weight of what he did.
A burning bush doesn’t erase a bloody past.
Grace does.

When God speaks in Exodus 3, He doesn’t say,
“Moses, prove you’ve changed.”

He says,
“I have seen the suffering… and I am sending you.”
Sending.
A former murderer.
This is the scandal of grace:

God doesn’t build His kingdom with perfect people.
He builds it with surrendered ones.

Yes, sin is real.
Yes, justice matters.
Moses’ act was wrong—no excuses.
But sin doesn’t get the final word.
Jesus does.

Because centuries later, another Deliverer would come—
not with hidden sin…
but to carry ours.

Jesus Christ didn’t bury bodies in the sand—
He was buried for ours.
And then He walked out of the grave.
Alive.

So your past?
It’s not your identity.

Repent.
Turn.
Bring it into the light.

Because the same God who met Moses in the wilderness
meets you right where you are.
Not to shame you—
but to send you.
Someone you know is still running from their past.
